TITLE DETAIL
Rename and Delete sit at the foot of the screen, under the facts card, built from the same row the Settings screen uses. Neither carries a chevron: a chevron means a way in, and these open dialogs. The flow reads left to right and ends back in Browse with the row gone.

BROWSE
Hold a row to select, exactly as today. The bar keeps its count and its one red Download; the three new verbs get a second line. Rename greys out unless exactly one thing is picked. NOTE FOR BUILD: this makes the bar ~144px, not the 92px SELECTION_BAR_HEIGHT exports today — that constant and the list's bottom padding both have to grow, or the last row hides under it.
The red FILL stays on Download — one per screen, per the design system. Delete carries the accent on its glyph only. The red button appears where it belongs: in the confirm dialog.

FOLDERS: DOWNLOAD ONLY.
Move, rename and delete are for FILES. Folders keep their pick box and keep feeding Download exactly as they do today — so the moment a folder joins the pick, the three new verbs go dead and the bar's detail line says why, while Download stays live. Nothing about the existing download behaviour changes.

Delete has no Undo — it is a real unlink, so the modal is the only gate. That is why its copy names the size and what else goes: the chapters you wrote and where you left off. Only files reach this dialog, so it never has to explain a subtree.

Grounded in the SMB probe (17 Sep): each file's move is ONE metadata operation — 32 MB moved in 7 ms — so a batch is N independent renames and a dropped share leaves each file either moved or not, never half-moved. That is what this notice can honestly promise, and why Undo is cheap: the inverse is the same rename back.
